newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on peso jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate closes up on peso jitters.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate reversed early gains in late trade but still closed up 35 basis points at 28.60 percent on Wednesday, after a volatile session dominated by a shaky peso.
"We were closely linked to the forex market today. Panic spread in the morning and shook secondary money market rates," a trader said.
The overnight rate reached a high of 29.90 percent at midsession.
The benchmark 48-hour peso staggered to close six centavos weak at 7.84/7.85 per dollar after a speculative battering.
"The surge in overnight rates was checked by banks stepping in to buy paper, and when the peso recouped some lost ground," another trader said.

Many traders said the initial bout of speculation was triggered by comments made by M.I.T. economics professor Rudiger Dornbusch in the local press, which quoted him as saying that the peso needed to be devalued by 20 percent, to nine per dollar.

Dornbusch was later quoted as saying by Banco Santander that a year-end exchnage rate of eight per dollar would be adequate to compensate for inflation. Traders added that Tuesday night's hikes in primary Cetes rates were not enough to ease pressure on the unsteady peso, and noted that term instruments were under most pressure on Wednesday.
In the secondary market, 28-day Cetes closed up 100 basis points at 29.00 percent, compared to the primary rate of 27.70 percent assigned on Tuesday.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed 65 basis points down at 29.75 percent.
Liquidity shortages on Thursday were expected from credit maturities totalling 1.50 billion pesos, and an oversupply of 716 million pesos carried over from Tuesday's primary auction.
